ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Friedrich Nietzsche

code.originalText: Eight-week review of prevention: headache days, disability, mood, sleep and the plan ahead

text.paragraph: Eight-week review of migraine prevention after the withdrawal. [S]

Mr. Nietzsche returns eight weeks after starting galcanezumab and five weeks after the last butalbital tablet. His diary shows 7 headache days in the past four weeks, 4 with migraine features, and no attack lasting more than a day. He used acute medicine on 5 days: sumatriptan on 3, with relief within two hours in 2, and naproxen on 2. He has taken no combination tablets. The injections cause only brief redness, and his constipation is unchanged. The floaters in his right eye have nearly gone, with no new flashes. He sleeps about six hours after five CBT-I sessions. His mood is good. His HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B tests from the preventive visit were negative, and he was told by phone. He is writing for several hours on most days and walking as before. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-15; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Repeat dilated examination of the right eye: the vitreous detachment is complete, with no retinal break or detachment; macula unchanged

Frequent disabling headaches on about 20 days a month, with nausea, vomiting and light sensitivity, mostly right-sided, since childhood and more frequent over the past year, with a combination headache tablet containing butalbital taken on about 16 days a month; under evaluation with a headache diary, MRI, syphilis serology and a headache medicine consultation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented headaches; superseded when the consultation confirmed chronic migraine with medication overuse headache.

Chronic migraine without aura (15 or more headache days a month for more than three months, at least 8 with migraine features); ICHD-3 criteria met in a two-week diary; MRI of the brain normal; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented headaches, which historians interpret differently
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation; the historical diagnosis is disputed (CLM-0014), so this is not a claim about his real diagnosis.

Medication overuse headache from a butalbital, acetaminophen and caffeine combination on 10 or more days a month for more than three months, with ibuprofen on other days; resolved after a three-week taper and withdrawal
S — Synthetic diagnosis made at the consultation, anchored to his documented use of many medicines and sedatives; not a claim about his real medicines.
High myopia in both eyes, much worse in the right eye, since early childhood, with long-standing poor vision in the right eye and unequal pupils; comprehensive eye examination booked
S — Synthetic modern coding of his documented severe myopia.

Pathologic (degenerative) myopia of the right eye with patchy chorioretinal atrophy of the macula, a posterior staphyloma and a tilted optic disc; no choroidal neovascularization on OCT; best corrected vision 20/100 in the right eye
S — Synthetic finding of the comprehensive eye examination, anchored to his documented poor right eye and the retrospective reading of it as myopic degeneration; not a claim about his real eyes.
Chronic insomnia, with difficulty falling asleep and early waking, worse on headache nights; no sleep medicine at intake
S — Synthetic sleep problem anchored to his documented severe insomnia; not a claim about his real sleep.
Acute posterior vitreous detachment of the right eye, with flashes and a floater, without a retinal break, detachment or vitreous hemorrhage on dilated examination, in an eye with pathologic myopia
S — Synthetic acute eye problem in a highly myopic eye; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Chronic migraine without aura on galcanezumab (G43.709). A good early response: headache days down from about 20 to 7 and migraine days from about 12 to 4 in four weeks, so he no longer has headache on 15 or more days a month. The MIDAS of 31 still counts the weeks before treatment and the withdrawal weeks in its three-month recall. Efficacy will be judged formally at three months. [S]
Third galcanezumab injection, 120 mg, today.
Three-month review in four weeks, before he leaves for the winter; plan to continue for at least six to twelve months.
OnabotulinumtoxinA as the next option if the response fades.

Medication overuse headache (G44.40). Resolved: no overuse for five weeks and headache days well below 15 a month. [S]
Keep acute medicine to no more than eight days a month.

Posterior vitreous detachment, right eye (H43.811). Complete detachment without a break; symptoms resolved. [S]
Yearly dilated examination; same-day eye care for new warning symptoms.

Chronic insomnia (G47.00). Sleep lengthening with CBT-I. [S]
Finish the CBT-I course.
